document: P9 GENERATION 1 — PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE HEAD IS REFIT (理
written_at: 2026-09-17, while the cost limb was still running. G1 does not exist and no refit has been computed. Nothing here was chosen after seeing a G1 number.
what_P9_asks: does the prior ACCUMULATE? A second generation learns from a better agent's episodes. If each generation must be trained from the base agent's play, the method is a one-shot improvement; if generations compound, it is the thing the paper exists for.

the_design.G0: the head fit on seed 47's 300 post-inspect states, run on seed 21's full 300. This IS the cost-limb run -- G0 is not a separate experiment.
the_design.G1: a head refit on G0's OWN post-inspect states and outcomes from that run. The second generation learns from the episodes a better agent produced.
the_design.evaluation: on seed 47's 75, against G0-on-47 (29.3%, 9.81 actions) and the base (17.3%, 10.68). Same 75 problems, paired.
the_design.THE_LABELS: come from the VERIFIER -- whether the region a candidate names is the true bug_region -- and NEVER from the head's own picks. A head trained on its own choices learns to agree with itself, which would produce a rising number that means nothing. 理, and it is the single most important line in this file.

THE_THREE_READINGS.PASS: G1 >= G0 on seed 47 at no higher cost. Accumulation does not degrade -- a second generation can be trained on a better agent's play without losing what the first had.
THE_THREE_READINGS.STRONG: G1 > G0 by more than 1 SE (SE at n=75 is ~5.3 points, so > ~5.3 points). The prior COMPOUNDS, and that is the claim the programme was built to test.
THE_THREE_READINGS.FAIL: G1 < G0. The second generation forgets or overfits its parent -- the episodes of a better agent are a WORSE training signal than the base agent's, which would say the method is one-shot and name why.

the_constraint: G1 >= the base (17.3%) with nothing lost per §4.2a. A G1 below the base is a capability failure regardless of how it compares to G0.
what_I_expect_and_why_it_is_written_down: I expect PASS rather than STRONG. G0's episodes contain FEWER failures to learn from -- it solves more and burns fewer actions -- so the second generation trains on a smaller and easier pool of post-inspect decisions. Accumulation by compounding would need the better agent's decisions to be more INFORMATIVE, not merely better, and nothing measured so far says they are.
bounds: n = 75 for the evaluation, SE ~5.3 points. STRONG needs > 1 SE and is therefore a high bar at this n; that is deliberate.

G1 is trained on G0's states, which were produced with a head in the loop. The states are therefore not identically distributed to the base agent's -- that IS the experiment, and it is also the reason a naive comparison of head accuracies between generations would not be meaningful.
One model, one layer, one grammar. Two seeds.

POOL_STATISTICS_TO_PRINT_BESIDE_THE_READ.why: 理: 'a smaller and easier pool' is my READING of why I expect PASS rather than STRONG. It has to be a NUMBER beside the result, or the reading explains whatever happens.
measured for BOTH training pools: fraction drawn from episodes that FAILED
fraction where the TRUE region was among the candidates (the ceiling on what the pool can teach)
POOL_STATISTICS_TO_PRINT_BESIDE_THE_READ.how_it_changes_the_reading: if G1's pool is smaller and skewed toward SUCCESSES, then a PASS is 'accumulation survives a weaker training signal' and a FAIL is 'the signal got weaker', and those are different conclusions from the same number. Printing the pools is what separates them.

POOLS_MEASURED_BEFORE_THE_G1_NUMBER_EXIS.AND_HALF_MY_STATED_REASON_IS_ALREADY_WRO: I predicted PASS-not-STRONG because G1 would train on 'a smaller and easier pool'. It is NOT SMALLER -- both pools are 300 decisions over 300 distinct programs, because every episode contributes exactly one post-inspect decision whether it succeeds or fails. It IS easier: 68.3% of G1's decisions come from failed episodes against 83.3% of G0's. So the mechanism I named is half right, and the half that is wrong was a guess about size that one count refuted. This is why 理 asked for the numbers rather than the reading.
POOLS_MEASURED_BEFORE_THE_G1_NUMBER_EXIS.what_it_does_to_the_reading: a PASS now reads as 'accumulation survives a 15-point shift toward successes in the training pool', and a FAIL reads as 'that shift was enough to cost it'. Neither reads as 'the pool ran out of data'.
